'''Business and economy'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**The [[Parler]] [[social networking service]] goes offline after [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] discontinued providing [[cloud computing]] services. The company's [[chief executive]] said that the service will be down "longer than expected" as "most people with enough servers to host us have shut their doors to us." [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/11/parler-drops-offline-after-amazon-withdraws-support.html (CNBC)]
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
**[[Ford Motor Company]] announces that it will cease production at its plants in [[Camaçari]] and [[Taubaté]] in the coming months due to losses aggravated by the pandemic. Ford also plans to close its [[Troller Veículos Especiais|Troller]] plant in [[Belo Horizonte]] in the fourth quarter of 2021. [https://www.deccanherald.com/business/covid-19-ford-to-close-all-its-factories-in-brazil-938054.html (AFP via ''Deccan Herald'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sriwijaya Air Flight 182]]
**[[Indonesia]]n authorities identify the first victim of the [[Sriwijaya Air]] [[Boeing 737 Classic|Boeing 737-500]] that crashed into the [[Java Sea]], a 29-year-old male [[flight attendant]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/indonesian-plane-crash-rescuers-identify-first-victim/a-56193681 (DW)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]] announces that a [[World Health Organization]] team investigating the origins of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] will arrive in the country on Thursday. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20210111-china-says-who-experts-to-probe-covid-19-origins-during-visit-starting-thursday (France 24)]
****[[Mainland China]] reports 103 new cases in the past 24 hours, mainly in [[Hebei]] [[provinces of China|province]], which is the highest single-day total since July 30 and brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 87,536. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/china-hebei-covid-19-new-cases-most-since-july-shijiazhuang-13935150 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Malaysia]]
*****The [[Government of Malaysia|government]] signs a deal with [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]] to buy an additional 12.2 million doses of the [[tozinameran]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/01/11/moh-pfizer-sign-manufacturing-and-supply-agreement-for-covid-19-vaccine (''The Star'')]
****[[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] announces a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in the federal territories of [[Kuala Lumpur]], [[Labuan]] and [[Putrajaya]] as well as in five [[States and federal territories of Malaysia|state]]s and also bans interstate travel for two weeks beginning January 13 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://amp.scmp.com/week-asia/health-environment/article/3117269/coronavirus-malaysian-prime-minister-muhyiddin-yassin (''South China Morning Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
*****The [[National Agency of Drug and Food Control of Republic of Indonesia|Food and Drug Supervisory Agency]] approves [[Sinovac]]'s [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for emergency use in the [[Indonesia|country]]. This comes after a clinical trial showed the vaccine had a 65.3% efficacy in Indonesia compared to an efficacy of 91% in [[Turkey]] and 78% in [[Brazil]]. [https://jakartaglobe.id/news/indonesia-approves-sinovac-vaccine-amid-dramatic-surge-in-coronavirus-cases (''Jakarta Globe'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination program in the Philippines]]
*****The [[Philippines]] orders 25 million doses of [[Sinovac]]'s [[vaccine]]. 50,000 doses of the vaccine are expected to arrive in the country by February. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1382086/ph-secures-25-m-covid-19-vaccines-from-chinas-sinovac-50k-doses-coming-in-feb (''Inquirer'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon]]
****[[Lebanon]] declares a [[state of emergency]] and imposes a 24-hour curfew for 11 days beginning January 14 as part of a lockdown that began on January 7. All private and public companies as well as house of worships will be closed with few exceptions and travel restrictions will also be introduced. [http://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/Lebanon-News/2021/Jan-11/516208-lebanon-declares-state-of-emergency-to-contain-virus.ashx (''The Daily Star'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Albania]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Albania]]
*****[[Albania]] begins its vaccination programme against COVID-19 with doses received from an undisclosed [[European Union]] country. [[Prime Minister of Albania|Prime Minister]] [[Edi Rama]] is among the first to receive the vaccine. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/albania-carries-1st-vaccinations-donated-doses-75177352 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****The [[Netherlands]] detects at least 30 cases of a new variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in an outbreak linked to a primary school in [[Bergschenhoek]]. [https://www.dutchnews.nl/news/2021/01/municipality-to-test-60000-residents-for-british-strain-of-coronavirus/ (Dutch News)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record 122 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 7,925. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/portugals-president-72-tests-positive-for-coronavirus/2021/01/12/59f8c3ac-54ba-11eb-acc5-92d2819a1ccb_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
****[[President of Portugal|President]] [[Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa]] tests positive for COVID-19. He is self-isolating in [[Belém Palace]] asymptomatic. [https://www.publico.pt/2021/01/11/politica/noticia/marcelo-teste-positivo-covid19-1945923/amp (''PÚBLICO'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Seychelles]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Africa#Seychelles|COVID-19 vaccination in Seychelles]]
*****[[Seychelles]] becomes the first African country to begin vaccination campaign against COVID-19. One of the first to receive the vaccine is the president [[Wavel Ramkalawan]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2021/01/10/seychelles-begins-covid-immunisation-campaign/ (Africa News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] reports a record 3,074 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide case total to 162,350. [https://www.reuters.com/article/healthcoronavirus-tunisia/tunisia-reports-daily-coronavirus-record-of-3074-cases-idUSL1N2JM29W (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]	
****The [[Government of Zimbabwe|government]] orders that victims of COVID-19 must be buried where they die, forbidding [[Viewing (funeral)|viewings]] and the transfer of corpses as the country experiences a significant increase in the number of cases. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/11/c_139658958.htm (Xinhua)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delaware]]
*****[[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] receives a second dose of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[vaccine]] on camera. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/11/politics/biden-second-dose-coronavirus-vaccine/index.html (CNN)]
****The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] says it has administered 8 million [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] doses in the [[United States]] and distributed an additional 25.5 million doses. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-usa-cdc/25-5-mln-doses-of-covid-19-vaccines-distributed-nearly-9-mln-administered-u-s-cdc-idUSL4N2JM38T (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****Two [[gorilla]]s in the [[San Diego Zoo Safari Park]] test positive for [[COVID-19]], making this the first case of transmission to non-human [[primate]]s or [[great ape]]s. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-01-11/gorillas-contract-coronavirus-at-san-diego-zoo-safari-park (''The Los Angeles Times'')]
****The state surpasses 30,000 deaths from COVID-19, just a month after surpassing 20,000 deaths. [https://apnews.com/article/california-coronavirus-pandemic-b7f064ee30979fae67170b229db1c6b9 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indiana]], Variant of Concern 202012/01
****[[Indiana]] reports its first case of a new variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] from the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.indystar.com/story/news/health/2021/01/11/indiana-finds-cases-new-coronavirus-strain-which-spreads-easily/6624127002/ (''Indystar'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***Lockdowns in [[Brisbane]] and the [[Northern Beaches]] of [[Sydney]] are lifted as the number of cases in those areas drop. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-01-10/northern-beaches-reopen-after-three-week-covid-lockdown/13045954 (ABC Australia)] [https://www.9news.com.au/videos/health/greater-brisbane-lockdown-lifted/ckjsb7qp4001s0gpcpn4nobz8 (9 News)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[BioNTech]] says it plans to produce two billion vaccine doses this year. [https://thehill.com/changing-america/well-being/prevention-cures/533643-biontech-aims-to-produce-2-billion-vaccine-doses (''The Hill'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan]]
***[[Uzbekistan]] extends their travel restrictions to the [[United Kingdom]], [[Italy]], [[Denmark]], [[Austria]], [[Australia]], the [[Netherlands]], and [[South Africa]] until February 1. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/11/c_139659239.htm (Xinhuanet)]  
*[[United States–Yemen relations]]
**The leader of the [[Houthi movement]], [[Mohammed Ali al-Houthi]], condemns a move by the United States to designate the group as "terrorists" saying that the group "reserves its right to respond to any designation" by the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]. Iran and the [[Norwegian Refugee Council]] also condemn the designation, saying that it will create more devastation in the impoverished nation. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/11/yemens-houthis-condemn-us-move-to-brand-them-terrorists (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Cuba–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] declares [[Cuba]] a [[State Sponsors of Terrorism (U.S. list)|State Sponsor of Terrorism]]. Cuba was removed from the list by the [[Presidency of Barack Obama|Obama administration]] in 2015 during the [[Cuban thaw]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/u-s-declares-cuba-state-sponsor-terrorism-n1253770 (NBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[2021 efforts to remove Donald Trump from office]]
***[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] in the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] introduce an [[Impeachment in the United States#Articles of impeachment|article of impeachment]] against Trump for "incitement of insurrection". [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/house-democrats-file-impeachment-article-charging-trump-incitement/story?id=75178177 (ABC News)]
**The [[New York State Bar Association]] announces that it has launched an inquiry into removing [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s attorney [[Rudy Giuliani]] from its membership over his role in the "[[January 6 United States Capitol attack|violent uprising]]" at the [[United States Capitol|Capitol building]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-01-11/giuliani-may-be-expelled-from-n-y-bar-group-over-capitol-riot (Bloomberg)]
**[[Yogananda Pittman]] is named as acting [[United States Capitol Police]] chief, making her the first woman and first [[African Americans|African-American]] to lead the agency. [https://www.npr.org/sections/congress-electoral-college-tally-live-updates/2021/01/11/955598516/in-historic-first-u-s-capitol-police-name-yogananda-pittman-as-acting-chief (NPR)]
*Three police officers are killed, two by gunfire and one in a hit-and-run, after a carjacking in [[Isla Verde, Puerto Rico]]. A fourth police officer is also injured. This is the first time in Puerto Rico's recent history in which multiple police officers were killed in one incident. The suspect remains at large. [https://apnews.com/article/puerto-rico-shootings-police-latin-america-512a797c046c60b15f0fc0b95f228384 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020–21 United States election protests]]
**An internal bulletin by the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] warns of nationwide armed [[2021 United States inauguration week protests|protests]] being planned from January 16 to 20, the day of [[Inauguration of Joe Biden|Joe Biden's inauguration]]. The bulletin also warned of an armed group threatening to start a "huge uprising" if there is an attempt to remove Donald Trump from [[President of the United States|office]] via the [[Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution|25th Amendment]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/armed-protests-planned-50-state-capitols-fbi-bulletin/story?id=75179771 (ABC News)] [https://apnews.com/article/joe-biden-politics-inaugurations-capitol-siege-ec75b26289166b4afd30c15b0dd2ded5 (AP)]
**[[Airbnb]] says it will ban bookings for hate groups and rioters in [[Washington, D.C.]] ahead of Biden's inauguration. [https://www.cnet.com/news/airbnb-combs-dc-bookings-for-hate-groups-before-inauguration/ (CNET)] [https://www.washingtonian.com/2021/01/11/airbnb-announces-plan-to-prevent-capitol-rioters-hate-group-members-from-using-its-platform-during-inauguration/ (''Washingtonian'')]
**[[Michigan]] announces it will ban open-carry guns at the [[Michigan State Capitol|state capitol]]. [https://www.huffpost.com/entry/michigan-open-carry-ban-capitol_n_5ffc978cc5b66f3f796029fc (''HuffPost'')]
**President Trump approves an [[state of emergency|emergency]] declaration request from [[Mayor of the District of Columbia|District of Columbia Mayor]] [[Muriel Bowser]] ahead of Biden's inauguration. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/01/11/donald-trump-dc-state-of-emergency-inauguration-457890 (''Politico'')] [https://www.foxnews.com/us/trump-emergency-dc-biden-inauguration (Fox News)]
**[[Chad Wolf]] [[List of Trump administration dismissals and resignations|resigns]] as Acting [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security]], citing "recent events, including the ongoing and meritless court rulings regarding the validity of my authority as Acting Secretary". He is replaced by [[Federal Emergency Management Agency|FEMA]] Administrator [[Pete Gaynor]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/jan/11/chad-wolf-resigns-acting-us-homeland-security-secretary (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Pope Francis]] publishes an apostolic letter in which, modifying the [[canon law]], opens officially ministries of lector and [[acolyte]] to women. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/pope-francis-opens-ministries-of-lector-and-acolyte-to-women-a-cna-explainer-28784 (Catholic News Agency)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election]]
**[[Facebook]] bans "Stop the Steal" content ahead of Biden's [[Inauguration of Joe Biden|inauguration]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/facebook-bans-all-stop-steal-content-n1253809 (NBC News)]
**[[Twitter]] says that they have [[Twitter suspensions|suspended]] over 70,000 accounts linked to the [[QAnon]] conspiracy since the [[2021 United States Capitol attack|Capitol storming]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/11/twitter-has-suspended-70000-qanon-accounts-since-us-capitol-riot-.html (CNBC)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Bill Belichick]], the head coach of the [[New England Patriots]], declines the [[Presidential Medal of Freedom]] from [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], citing the [[2021 storming of the United States Capitol|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]]. He had been scheduled to receive it on Thursday. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/11/politics/bill-belichick-presidential-medal-of-freedom-spt-trnd/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[2020–21 NBA season]]
**The [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] announces that they have postponed Monday night’s matchup between [[Dallas Mavericks]] and [[New Orleans Pelicans]], and Tuesday match between [[Boston Celtics]] and [[Chicago Bulls]] due to COVID-19 health protocols. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/11/sports/basketball/nba-postponed-mavericks-celtics.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[2021 College Football Playoff National Championship]]
**In [[American football]], [[2020 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama]] defeats [[2020 Ohio State Buckeyes football team|Ohio State]] to win the national championship. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/sports/no-1-alabama-wins-national-title-over-no-3-ohio-n1253849 (NBC News)]
